summary: FRONTEND-ONLY test of the new Solutions subject tabs + horizontal question rail and the sitewide visual refresh. Results/Solutions used fully mocked API data via Playwright route interception: a fake session in the script only, every non-GET fulfilled locally, no real DB writes and no AI calls. Fixtures: JEE 75Q/3 subjects, BITSAT 130Q/5 subjects + 12 bonus, Mathematics chapter 50Q. Tested at 1920x800 and 390x844. CORE SOLUTIONS FUNCTIONALITY PASSES. Only one question opens by default. The Solutions panel has no dropdown, previous/next, load more or accordion; the only combobox is the existing Reflection category Select. Switching subject updates only that subject's row and opens its first matching question (Maths -> Q51). The last number is reachable at 390px: Q50 in the chapter rail, Q75 in the JEE Maths rail and Q130 by deep link. Question numbers stay paired with their supplied solutions (Q1/Q75/Q81 show 'Supplied solution · Qn'). Outcome filters (incorrect, marked, dropped, bonus, bonus-section, all) apply only to the selected subject. Subject tabs with 0 matches can still be tapped and show an honest empty state. Changing the filter keeps the selected question if it still matches, otherwise picks the first match. Arrow keys move focus and selection between subject tabs; rail buttons show a 3px focus outline and Enter selects them. Back/forward works. score_version=gv2 stays in the URL and is sent to the API. Clicking a heat-map cell in Analysis resets a non-matching filter to 'all' and switches to the right subject. Solution-open tracking: posted once per newly visited question (no repeats), no AI GETs, score unchanged. A failed tracking call shows the retry button, which works and re-enables the 'reviewed solution' checkbox. Neither Refresh evidence nor a saved reflection locks tracking. Results stays forced light when dark mode is preferred. No page-level horizontal overflow (document.scrollWidth == innerWidth) anywhere we checked: Results (both widths), and Home, /exams, series hub, login, owner-login, home, 3 exam hubs, chapters, mocks, results, my-tests, competitions and studio in light and dark at both widths. The rail overflows only inside its own overflow-x:auto container. Logo /brand/jeelive-logo.webp (980x407, 8-10px padding, nothing cropped) and favicon jeelive-icon.png load locally with 200 and are not cut off in header or footer. The Babel plugin fix (importPath.parentPath.traverse) compiles; the latest webpack run has 1 warning, in Profile.js only, and Results.js has no hook warnings. Main problem found: the new colourful styling for the filter tabs and exam-destination tabs does not apply in preview, and the active filter tab does not get the accent in production either (CSS specificity and the visual-edits wrapper, see RCA).

ui_bugs.issue: vibrant-ui.css .filter-tabs>button rules (colours, 12px font, per-outcome --tab-accent, solid active state) are never applied in preview. Computed style is the browser default 16px font, transparent background, pill radius 999px, and a pale brand-soft active state (see RCA). In production the child combinator works, but simple-navigation.css:275-276 (.results-page .filter-tabs button / button.active, which has higher specificity) still overrides the active state, so the active filter never shows its solid red/green/amber accent. This makes them inconsistent with the bold subject/result tabs.

Same cause: in preview, the .exam-destinations>a rules and the nth-child(2)/(3) amber/green accents do not match, because each <a> sits in its own <span data-ve-dynamic style='display:contents'> wrapper. Result: plain dark text links with a pale active state. Any mapped children styled with > or :nth-child are at risk: .studio-tabs>button, .segmented>button, .ai-review-filters>button and .jeelive-tabs .jeelive-tab:nth-child(n). Preview will not match production.

integration_issues.flow: Solutions deep link with conflicting params
integration_issues.issue: /results/:id?view=solutions&subject=Physics&question=q60 (q60 is a Maths question) silently replaces the question with Physics Q1. A valid explicit question should probably win and its subject be taken from it; requestedSubject currently takes precedence (Results.js line 90).

The score-version-original and score-version-{n} buttons call nav('/results/'+id+'?score_version=...'). This drops view, subject, question and filter, so the user is sent back to Analysis and loses their place in Solutions.
An invalid filter value (e.g. filter=weird) is treated as 'all' but stays in the URL. The normalising effect only rewrites subject and question.

issues: The 'Matched to this frozen version' badge is rendered in Title Case ('Matched To This Frozen Version') and is very small (~8px) beside the solution title, especially on mobile.
On mobile the outcome filter row (16px pills) looks visually heavier and stylistically different from the compact coloured subject tabs above it; this goes away once the CSS bug is fixed.

Info: logged-in pages (/home, exam hubs, chapters) have the logo in the header only and a text-only footer ('© 2026 JEELIVE.AI'); public pages show the logo in both header and footer. Check this is intended.

action_items: Fix filter-tab styling. Either change vibrant-ui.css to use descendant selectors with enough specificity (e.g. .results-page .filter-tabs button, .results-page .filter-tabs button.active, .results-page .filter-tabs button[data-testid=...]), or remove/align simple-navigation.css lines 275-276 so the active filter gets its solid --tab-accent. Re-check in preview after the change.

Avoid the child combinator (>) and :nth-child for elements rendered via .map(). The dev visual-edits wrapper breaks them in preview: .exam-destinations>a, .studio-tabs>button, .segmented>button, .ai-review-filters>button, .jeelive-tabs .jeelive-tab:nth-child(n), .solution-legend>span:nth-child. Use explicit tone classes or data attributes, as already done for result-view tabs and subject tabs.
Optional: when the question param is valid but belongs to another subject, derive the subject from the question. Normalise invalid filter values out of the URL.
Optional: keep view=solutions, subject, question and filter when switching score version.
critical_code_review_comments: Results.js openQuestion re-implements the matchesOutcome logic inline (line 117); use matchesOutcome(question, filter) to avoid drift.

SolutionNavigator uses data-testid 'solution-question-'+number. If any paper restarts numbering per subject, test IDs would collide across subjects (functionally fine because buttons are keyed by id).
Results.js is 579 lines; the inline JSX for the solution card could be extracted into a SolutionCard component.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Fixture recipe: /app/tests/frontend_iter125_solutions_fixture.md. Gotchas: question-reports must return [] and review.categories must be strings, otherwise the error boundary shows 'We couldn't open this screen'. Results forces the exam-light class, so dark mode is irrelevant there. The visual-edits plugin wraps mapped JSX children in span[data-ve-dynamic] with display:contents, so CSS > and :nth-child selectors fail in preview only.
rca of the issue: Filter and destination tabs look unstyled in preview. Root cause: the dev-only Babel visual-edits plugin (plugins/visual-edits/babel-metadata-plugin.js, data-ve-dynamic) wraps every .map() child in <span data-ve-dynamic='true' style='display:contents'>. DOM check: document.querySelector('[data-testid=results-filter-all]').matches('.filter-tabs > button') === false. So vibrant-ui.css lines 46-67 never match in preview. Separately, simple-navigation.css:276 '.results-page .filter-tabs button.active' (specificity 0,3,1) beats vibrant '.filter-tabs>button.active' (0,2,1), so even in production the active filter stays pale brand-soft. To reproduce: open /results/:id?view=solutions at 390 or 1920 and check getComputedStyle on [data-testid=results-filter-incorrect] (16px, rgba(0,0,0,0), 999px). Fix: use descendant selectors or explicit classes with higher specificity, and drop the conflicting simple-navigation rules.
